sections.title: Revenue Ramp & Cash Burn
sections.subtitle: The two things that actually decide this stock: is revenue compounding fast enough, and is cash running out first?

charts.title: Revenue Ramp
charts.annotation: FY2022 $0.024m → FY2023 $0.358m → FY2024 $0.086m (real dip, not an error) → FY2025 $1.511m. H1 FY2026 $1.334m vs H1 FY2025 $0.694m is +92% YoY at the half.

charts.title: Operating Cash Burn vs Cash on Hand — the Survival Clock
charts.annotation: The single most important chart on the page. Burn has shrunk every period (FY2023 -$5.92m → FY2024 -$3.74m → FY2025 -$2.79m → H1 FY2026 -$1.52m) but cash was only $0.241m at 30 June 2025, rebuilt to $2.166m solely by the Dec-2025 capital raise. Going concern is explicitly conditional on hitting revenue forecasts and completing the Gisborne facility sale.

charts.title: Net Income
charts.annotation: FY2024's -$13.72m is an impairment (~$8.5m+ of goodwill/PP&E written down after the owned-cultivation strategy failed), not an operational collapse — the cash-burn chart above is the better read on operational trajectory. The company has never reported a profit in any period on record.

sections.title: Dilution & Balance Sheet
sections.subtitle: Serial, deeply discounted capital raises are central to the investment case — not a footnote.

charts.title: Shares Outstanding
charts.annotation: 17.0m pre-IPO (FY2020) → 140.3m post-listing (FY2021) → 158.1m (FY2023) → 159.8m (FY2024) → 223.6m (FY2025) → 338.0m (H1 FY2026): +112% in the 18 months to Dec-2025 alone. Warrants struck as low as $0.015 (below the $0.035 price) confirm the trend continues. Log scale shows the pre-IPO step without flattening the recent doublings.

charts.title: Shareholders' Equity
charts.annotation: $28.8m (FY2021) collapsing to $5.8m (H1 FY2026) — and even that printed figure is not audit-assured: it includes $2.195m goodwill and a $0.861m held-for-sale facility PwC could not corroborate in either the FY2024 or FY2025 disclaimer of opinion.

charts.title: Cash vs Total Debt
charts.annotation: Borrowings rose from $0.73m (30 Jun 2025) to $1.81m (31 Dec 2025) — short-tenor, warrant-sweetened working-capital and inventory finance, some related-party, rather than conventional bank debt.

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Sales of medicinal cannabis genetics and finished products (oils, dried flower) into Australia, New Zealand, Germany, the UK and Czechia via distributor and clinic-chain partners.

For Rua Bioscience: this is the bull case in one chart — revenue is compounding off a near-zero base at triple-digit YoY rates as the asset-light distribution pivot ramps. But absolute scale remains tiny: FY2025 total revenue of $1.51m is a rounding error against the $11.5-11.8m market cap, and the July-2026 UK deal (potentially $10m+ over two years) is unaudited, forward-looking and with an undisclosed partner.

What to watch:

  • Whether H1 FY2026's +92% YoY growth rate holds or decays as the base grows
  • Whether the UK deal starts converting to booked revenue in FY2027
  • Concentration — a small number of distribution partners per market means losing one is a material shock

runway.title: Operating Cash Burn vs Cash on Hand
runway.content:
Net cash used in operations each period, charted against cash and equivalents on the balance sheet at each period end.

For Rua Bioscience: this is the survival clock. Rua has never produced positive free cash flow in any period on record. Burn has shrunk consistently (FY2023 -$5.92m to H1 FY2026 -$1.52m), which is genuine operational progress, but cash was critically low ($0.241m at 30 June 2025) before the December 2025 raise rebuilt it to $2.166m. At the H1 FY2026 burn rate that implies roughly 7 months of runway on a balance sheet that is already 8 months stale (31 Dec 2025) at the analysis date. The Board's own going-concern statement makes survival explicitly conditional on (i) hitting revenue forecasts and (ii) completing the Gisborne facility sale, and states plainly that failing either may mean the Group cannot manage its minimum cash requirements.

What to watch:

  • Whether burn keeps shrinking half-on-half
  • Progress on the Gisborne facility sale — it has been "in progress" across multiple periods without completion
  • Any further capital raise, and at what price (recent raises have been at 40-50%+ discounts to VWAP)

netIncome.title: Net Income
netIncome.content:
Bottom-line statutory profit or loss.

For Rua Bioscience: Rua has never reported a profit. FY2024's -$13.72m loss is dominated by a non-cash impairment of goodwill and PP&E (~$8.5m+) following the failed owned-cultivation strategy, not a sudden operational deterioration — the operating cash flow chart is a cleaner read on the trend. NetMargin is intentionally not charted here: on a near-zero revenue base it produces meaningless figures like -31,302% (FY2022).

What to watch:

  • Whether losses narrow as revenue scales and the asset-light model's operating leverage kicks in
  • Any further impairment on the remaining $2.195m goodwill or the held-for-sale facility, both flagged as unauditable by PwC

dilution.title: Shares Outstanding
dilution.content:
Total ordinary shares on issue at each period end.

For Rua Bioscience: serial, deeply dilutive equity raising is one of the central risks in this stock, not a footnote. Shares on issue rose from 159.75m (30 June 2024) to 338.04m (31 December 2025) — a +112% increase in 18 months — and the pattern continues: 670,794 new warrants were issued in 2026 at a $0.015 strike, below even the current ~$0.035 share price. Accumulated losses of $42.76m against $48.17m of total capital ever raised mean roughly 89% of all shareholder capital contributed since listing has already been consumed. Every further raise at a tick-floor-adjacent price mechanically transfers a large share of the company to new money.

What to watch:

  • Any new placement, rights issue or warrant exercise announcement
  • The price at which new capital is raised relative to the market price
  • Whether the Gisborne facility sale reduces the need for further dilutive raises

equity.title: Shareholders' Equity
equity.content:
Total shareholders' equity (net assets) at each period end.

For Rua Bioscience: equity has collapsed from $28.8m (FY2021) to $5.8m (H1 FY2026), primarily via the FY2024 impairment. Critically, the printed figure is not audit-assured: PwC issued a disclaimer of opinion — the most severe audit outcome available — on both the FY2024 and FY2025 accounts, unable to corroborate the recoverability of $2.195m goodwill, $2.14m PP&E, $0.06m right-of-use assets and $0.861m assets held for sale (~$5.29m combined) underpinning the going-concern forecasts. A memo tangible-equity estimate (equity less goodwill less the held-for-sale facility) is closer to ~$2.8m, or roughly $0.008/share on the current diluted count.

What to watch:

  • Whether the FY2026 audit (due imminently) delivers a third consecutive disclaimer of opinion
  • Completion (or failure) of the Gisborne facility sale, which the held-for-sale asset depends on

cashDebt.title: Cash vs Total Debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash and equivalents against total borrowings at each period end.

For Rua Bioscience: net cash of ~$0.353m at 31 December 2025 should be treated as approximately zero given the figures are 8 months stale against an ongoing ~$1.5m-per-half burn rate. Borrowings more than doubled from $0.73m to $1.81m over H1 FY2026 alone — short-tenor working-capital, inventory-finance and supplier-finance arrangements, several carrying embedded warrant or VWAP-linked conversion features, with two directors among the inventory-finance lenders. This is expensive, related-party-linked financing, not conventional bank debt, and signals restricted access to cheaper capital.

What to watch:

  • Whether short-term debt keeps growing between capital raises
  • Conversion terms on any debt-linked warrants, which add further dilution risk on top of straight equity issuance
